verdict: Disney grew revenue 5% to $21.2B and segment profit jumped 86% to $3.0B — but $1.0B of impairment and restructuring charges cut the profit shareholders actually kept to just $264M.

kpis.note: excluding certain items; vs $0.30 a year ago

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.note: Writing down goodwill, an equity investment and licensed content, plus severance — see one-time items.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $282M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $227M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Of the $694M of net income, $430M belongs to noncontrolling interests, leaving $264M attributable to Disney (the $0.14 EPS figure). Costs are split between services and products using the fiscal 2023 10-K less the first nine months reported in the Q3 FY23 10-Q, since the earnings release reports one combined cost line; operating income of $1,062M is derived as revenue less those costs and the restructuring charge.

takeaways.title: Segment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Total segment operating income rose 86% to $2,976M: Experiences profit grew 31% to $1,759M on cruise ships, Vacation Club sales and international parks, Sports rose 14% to $981M, and Entertainment swung from a $608M loss to a $236M profit as streaming losses narrowed.

takeaways.title: Streaming added subscribers
takeaways.text: Disney+ added nearly 7 million core subscribers in the quarter, helped by Elemental, The Little Mermaid and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 arriving on the service, and Disney still expected streaming to reach profitability in Q4 of fiscal 2024.

takeaways.title: Charges held GAAP profit to $0.14
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was just $0.14 because of $1,021M of restructuring and impairment charges and Fox/Hulu purchase-accounting amortization. Excluding certain items, EPS was $0.82. Disney also raised its cost-cutting target to $7.5B a year.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $1,021M. The charges Disney excludes from its adjusted EPS ($965M net) included impairments of goodwill ($721M), an equity investment ($141M) and licensed content ($137M) plus $22M of severance, partly offset by a $56M gain related to A+E. Adjusted EPS of $0.82 also adds back $429M of amortization of the Fox (TFCF) and Hulu acquisition intangible assets.
